transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is sump / tub-to-pump hose. Next: Establish WHERE the water appears, WHEN in the cycle, and what it LOOKS like before choosing a part. Let me know what you find.
ok I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now, should I get out of it first?? the fuse box is in the hall and the floor's dry there. the water is mostly at the front under the door

Yes, step off the wet floor onto a dry area now, and don't touch the machine, the plug or the socket while water is near them. From the dry hall, switch off the main switch at the fuse box to cut power to the machine, and only come back to the kitchen once it's off. From what you have described, the most likely cause is door seal (boot). Is the leaking water clean, soapy/dirty wash water, or dirty/oily-looking water?
I'm out of the kitchen now, in the hall by the fuse box. The water looks like just normal clear wash water I think, no suds or dirt. Should I switch it off now?

Yes, but don't touch the machine, the plug or the socket while you're standing on the wet floor, because water has reached the plug. Step out of the water onto the dry hall floor and switch off the circuit at the fuse box. Next: If the door seal is ripped, check the drum for up/down play, a dropped drum or bearing noise so a replacement seal isn't destroyed too. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
ok I'm on the dry hall floor now, switching off the main switch at the fuse box. Do I leave the machine alone until it's checked? I haven't touched the plug or the socket.

Yes, leave the machine, plug and socket alone, and step off the wet floor, since the water has reached the plug and you're in socks. From the dry hall, switch off the power at the fuse box (the main switch or the kitchen circuit), and don't go near the machine until the power is off and the floor is dry. Next: If it started after cleaning the filter, re-seat the filter cap/seal and check the sealing face before suspecting the pump. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
ok the main switch is off now, I'm still in the hall and haven't gone back in. What should I do next?

Next: If there is a big leak with heavy banging, check for a loose counterweight / cracked tub. Let me know what you find.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
sorry I don't really understand that, the power's off now and I'm still in the hall. Is it safe to go back in the kitchen or should I just wait here and call someone?

With the power off at the fuse box, it's reasonably safe to go back in, but put on dry shoes rather than socks and leave the plug and socket alone. Keep the power off until everything around the socket is completely dry. Where does the water seem to come from - front, back or underneath - and does it start while filling, washing, or draining/spinning?

It's coming from the front, under the door, and it was mid-wash when I noticed it. Normal washing sounds, no burning smell. I'll put shoes on before going back in.
